chapter.title: The Case of Negative Space
chapter.subtitle: The final mystery lives in what the camera never showed.
chapter.description: The final mystery lives in what the camera never showed.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Locked display. Unbroken recording. Trophy gone when the light changed.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: Promoter advertised the original. The loan sheet says “image supplied.”

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: After the film-reel mess? This man learns lessons on a free trial.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Do not convict him by sequel. Check the room.

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Alice
scenes.text: The camera shows five chairs, but everybody remembers sitting somewhere important.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I was important. I held two coats.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Rebuild the row. The side seats face mirrors; only the middle three face the pedestal.

puzzle.title: Everybody remembers being VIP
puzzle.instruction: Rebuild five seats from left to right, facing the stage. Only seats 2, 3, and 4 had a direct view; the end seats faced mirrors. “Beside” means immediately adjacent.

pieces.label: Watson
pieces.detail: I sat at an end. Sherlock was to my right, somewhere.

pieces.label: Alice
pieces.detail: I sat beside Watson, but not beside Promoter.

pieces.label: Sherlock
pieces.detail: I took the other end; I could reach the right aisle.

pieces.label: Promoter
pieces.detail: Cornball sat immediately to my left.

pieces.label: Cornball
pieces.detail: Alice and Promoter were my two neighbors.

hints: The two end witnesses orient the entire row.
Cornball must be in the middle, with Alice on his left.
puzzle.solvedText: Cornball and Promoter could see the real pedestal. Sherlock and Watson saw the side reflection. Their accounts describe different views of the same display.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

preDialogue.speaker: Alice
preDialogue.text: The curator has a demo table in front of the display. Clear the scheduled match and we can move the lights without a crowd blocking the lens.

preDialogue.speaker: Sherlock
preDialogue.text: Center district closes in round three. Like the sightline: keep another angle open.

postDialogue.speaker: Watson
postDialogue.text: Move the light left: trophy. Move it right: bare pedestal. It is a reflected painting.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: I paid VIP to look at a JPEG with furniture.

passive.name: Mirror Match
passive.description: The center district closes to new plays in round three.

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: The reflection explains the vanishing. It does not tell us where the brass original went. Follow the custody marks.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: Six handoffs. Every clerk swears their copy is the important one.

puzzle.title: Follow the brass, not the brochure
puzzle.instruction: Trace the original trophy from maker to final holder. Handoff codes connect OUT to IN. All six records belong in the chain. Photograph and replica notes do not transfer the brass object.

pieces.label: Maker
pieces.detail: Serial 041. OUT K8. Original brass trophy.

pieces.label: Courier
pieces.detail: IN P2 → OUT H9. Seal recorded intact.

pieces.label: Community hall
pieces.detail: IN H9. Serial 041 signed into the display cupboard; no outgoing record.

pieces.label: School
pieces.detail: IN K8 → OUT M3. Kept a paper rubbing.

pieces.label: Library
pieces.detail: IN M3 → OUT R6. Sent museum a photograph, not the trophy.

pieces.label: Repair shop
pieces.detail: IN R6 → OUT P2. Polished original serial 041.

hints: Start with the original’s maker; follow handoff codes.
The photograph branches off at the library. The original continues to the repair shop.
puzzle.solvedText: Serial 041 ends at the hall. The museum got a photograph. Its promise of an original was false before the supposed theft.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: The loan email said image supplied. I read “image” as “image of success.”

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: You read two words and financed a delusion.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Refunds were due tonight. I thought a theft would buy me a week.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: Instead you bought six witnesses. At retail.

tips: Read the clues, arrange the pieces, and use hints whenever you need them.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: He will call it an optical experience unless we can show exactly when he knew. Put the evidence in time order.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I have a dramatic finger ready.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: Keep it holstered.

puzzle.title: When did he know?
puzzle.instruction: Arrange the evidence by actual time, earliest first. Two devices use the wrong clock: printer is 10 minutes fast, camera is 5 minutes slow. The email and payment server use correct time.

pieces.label: First ticket sale — 14:06
pieces.detail: Payment-server time. Money accepted for the advertised original.

pieces.label: Poster print — 14:14
pieces.detail: Printer time. “SEE THE ORIGINAL.” Job approved by Promoter.

pieces.label: Theft announcement — 14:12
pieces.detail: Server time. Refund deadline postponed because of the alleged theft.

pieces.label: Spotlight moved — 14:04
pieces.detail: Camera time. Promoter turns the light away from the mirrored painting.

pieces.label: Loan email — 14:00
pieces.detail: Server time. “Photograph only; brass original remains at the hall.” Opened on Promoter’s account.

hints: Correct the printer and camera clocks before comparing entries.
The poster was printed at 14:04; the light moved at 14:09.
puzzle.solvedText: He opened the photograph-only email before approving the poster. Then he moved the light after collecting ticket money. This was concealment, not a misunderstanding.
puzzle.skipText: Your crew reconstructs the answer with you. The story and its rewards continue.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: The closing tournament is already sold out. Its door money covers the refunds if we finish the card.

preDialogue.speaker: Watson
preDialogue.text: Refund money goes straight to the desk. You get no handling fee.

preDialogue.speaker: Promoter
preDialogue.text: I had not even said handling.

preDialogue.speaker: Sherlock
preDialogue.text: Six rounds. The Opps gain a Motion in round four. Their crew has learned to save something for the end.

postDialogue.speaker: Watson
postDialogue.text: Tournament receipts cover the missing balance. The refund desk counted it in front of him.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: He tried to call the coins “micro-investments.” We made him count again.

starObjectives.description: Win all three districts against the final crew.

passive.description: At round four, The Opps gain 1 Motion.

scenes.speaker: Promoter
scenes.text: Real trophy is here. Signed loan, matching serial, refunds paid. Somebody put my face on the warning sign.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: It says CHECK THE DESCRIPTION.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Passenger the cart gets free entry. Only guest with a clean record.

tips: Read the district rules before committing your Motion.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: One fake train ride, one revenge broadcast, one trophy that never got stolen.

scenes.speaker: Sherlock
scenes.text: And every person said, “I can explain.” Eventually, we made them.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Put me down as associate detective.

scenes.speaker: Watson
scenes.text: You ate a receipt.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: It had barbecue sauce on it. Evidence expires.
